properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 17 at 6:14AM EDT until September 17 at 7:45AM EDT by NWS Northern Indiana
properties.description:
At 614 AM EDT, trained weather spotters reported thunderstorms
producing flash flooding in and around the Bluffton area in Wells
County. Localized rainfall estimates between 2 and 4 inches of rain
have fallen so far this morning on already saturated ground.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the warned
area.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Trained spotters reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Huntington, Bluffton, Decatur, Berne, Ossian, Geneva, Andrews,
Markle, Monroe, Lancaster, Preble, Nottingham, Zanesville,
Uniondale, Poneto, Vera Cruz, North Oaks, Murray, Kingsland and
Travisville.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued September 17 at 3:03AM PDT until September 17 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Elko NV
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING FOR FWZ 426 & 427 THURSDAY...

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire weather zones 426 and 427.

* WIND...Sustained southerly winds of 20-25 mph with gusts of
30-35 mph.

* HUMIDITY...Minimum afternoon values of 10-15%

* IMPACTS...any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A red flag warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.description:
FFWTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
North Central Pima County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 400 AM MST.

Milewide Road indicated a heavy flow of 2300 cfs (cubic feet per

will still result in flash flooding along and near the Brawley wash
as the water continues to drain into the early morning hours.

SOURCE...Gauges reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Tucson Estates and Picture Rocks.

This includes the following Flash Flood Prone Locations...
Manville Rd at Brawley Wash.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 16 at 9:14PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Citrus and Levy
Counties.

.The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon (US 41) has been steadily
rising since July and on September 15, reached flood stage. The cause
of the high water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is
excessive hydrilla growth (from river bottom to the water surface)
along a 4.5 mile stretch of river between US 41 and Lake Rousseau.
The hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing
water levels to rise.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and is forecast to continue.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:45 PM EDT Wednesday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:45 PM EDT Wednesday was 28.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 28.3 feet.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.4
feet on 08/25/2008.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at 200 PM EDT.
